diffs.diff: ozone ppm: datasheet reading gives 300 per count, the part's model has 1
diffs.evidence: The Winsen MQ131 (High Concentration) manual v1.6 defines no linear ppm-per-count or ppm-per-volt conversion. The 300 ppm figure is only the sensitivity test condition: 'Sensitivity S: Rs(in 300ppm O3) / Rs(in air) >= 2' and 'Output Voltage dVs: >=1.0V (in 300ppm O3)'. The manual's only formula is 'Rs=(Vc/VRL-1)xRL'. Concentration is read from Fig3, 'Typical Sensitivity Curve', a nonlinear log-log Rs/R0 chart where R0 is the resistance in clean air. Ozone raises Rs ('the sensor's conductivity gets lower along with the gas concentration rising'), so AO falls as ozone rises. A fixed scale of 300 ppm per count would be wrong in both size and sign. The model's scale of 1 belongs to the sim slider, which measures AO in volts (1 V per V on the AO pin), not ozone in ppm. The driver deliberately returns voltage, Rs and Rs/R0 for the user to calibrate, so the model is right.
